own_scenes.desc: Los DJs de club Mike Ross y Matt Dike, inspirados por Def Jam, montaron su sello con los Dust Brothers y un sampler SP-12. Tone Lōc, un Crip de voz inconfundible, y Young MC, estudiante de economía de USC venido de Queens que les rapeó por teléfono, escribieron juntos «Wild Thing» (1988, sobre «Jamie’s Cryin’» de Van Halen, cuatro millones de copias gracias a KROQ y KDAY) y «Funky Cold Medina»; Young MC triunfó con «Bust a Move», con Flea al bajo. Un hip hop de radio en plena época gangsta, y luego The Pharcyde (Bootie Brown, Fatlip, Imani, Slimkid3, con J-Swift y J Dilla): Bizarre Ride II the Pharcyde (1992) y «Passin’ Me By», los «Native Tongues bebés» de la Costa Oeste.

refs.q: They were kind of the anti–gangster rap.
refs.para: They were kind of the anti–gangster rap. They were talking about not getting the girl and the opposite of a lot of the macho, street posturing that was going on at the time. They were kind of the children of De La Soul, in a way. They were definitely coming from that place of Tribe, De La, Jungle Brothers—they had that irreverent, jazzy, hip-hop influence. They were the baby Native Tongues, the West Coast version.
